purpose: Transparent, pre-specified reference answer for the de-identified macro scenarios. It is a deliberately simple scoring rule, not a claim about the correct financial answer, and it is never shown to the model. It is used only for the accuracy comparison (C5) and the flip design; attribution and citation consistency are measured against the model's own behavior, not the rubric.

P.name: policy rate
P.+1: rate cut, or explicit easing bias
P.-1: rate hike, or explicit tightening bias

I.name: inflation
I.+1: falling and at, near or below target

G.name: growth and labor
G.+1: PMI at or above 50 and rising, or labor market improving
G.-1: PMI below 50, or unemployment rising / employment falling

E.name: earnings expectations
E.+1: consensus 12-month earnings forecasts revised up by 1% or more

F.name: financial conditions
F.+1: credit spreads narrowing or credit standards easing
F.-1: credit spreads widening or credit standards tightening

scoring: Each evidence record maps to exactly one component and receives -1, 0 or +1. The scenario score S is the sum over the records present.
decision: Positive if S >= +2; Negative if S <= -2; otherwise Neutral.
note_on_subsets: With thresholds of +/-2 no single record decides the signal alone, so the rubric answer for every single-record subset is Neutral. Subset-level rubric answers are reported descriptively only.
